title: Same Depth, Different Parents
statement:
You get the root of a binary tree whose node values are all distinct, and two different values x and y that both appear in it. The tree is given as values, so you identify the two nodes by value.

Return true if the two nodes are at the same depth and have different parents. Siblings (same parent) do not count, and neither do nodes at different depths.

examples.why: Both sit at depth 2; 4 hangs under 2 and 5 under 3.
Same depth, but both are children of 3. Checking only the depth gives the wrong answer.
Different parents, but 3 is at depth 1 and 4 at depth 2.

constraints: x ≠ y, both are values in the tree
hints: For each of the two values you need two facts. Which two?
Its depth and its parent's value. One walk over the tree can record both when it reaches x or y.
Or go level by level: at each level, see whether x and y both appear, and make sure they are not two children of one node.

explain.intuition:
The definition has two parts, so collect two facts per target: depth and parent. A depth-first walk that carries (depth, parent) down with it can record them when it meets x or y. Then compare: depths equal, parents different.

A breadth-first walk answers it level by level. While expanding a node, if its two children are exactly x and y, they are siblings and the answer is false. Otherwise, after a whole level, if both were seen in it, they are cousins; if only one was seen, they cannot be on the same level.
steps: Walk the tree, passing each node its depth and its parent's value.
When a node's value is x, store its depth and parent. Same for y.
pitfalls: Checking only the depth. Siblings share a depth but are not the answer.
Checking only the parents. Nodes with different parents can be at different depths.
Treating the root as having parent value 0 and then confusing it with a real node. Values here start at 1, but a sentinel like −1 or null is safer.

complexity.space: O(h) for recursion, or O(w) for the level queue

solutions.title: Depth-first, record depth and parent
solutions.idea: Carry depth and parent down the recursion; remember them for x and y; compare at the end.

solutions.title: Level by level
solutions.idea: Process one level at a time. Siblings are caught while expanding their parent; otherwise both must show up in the same level.

followups: Return all cousins of a given value x (same depth, different parent), in left-to-right order.
Values may repeat. How would you have to identify the two nodes instead?
